projects.title: World
projects.blurb: Walk, drive, sail or fly through a stylised version of the actual planet — real buildings, roads, rivers and terrain pulled from OpenStreetMap.
projects.readmeBlurb: A browser world whose structure is the real world — real buildings, roads, water, trees and terrain from OpenStreetMap — rendered in a crisp, stylized "old-game" look you can freely walk, drive, sail and fly through. Free for everyone, static-hostable on GitHub Pages, using only free/open data (OSM + free terrain). No Google, no paid APIs. Built on CesiumJS.

projects.title: TestForge
projects.blurb: A control plane for hardware and firmware test labs: see which devices are healthy, queue jobs across them, and triage crashes without SSHing into anything.
projects.readmeBlurb: Mission control for your test lab.

projects.title: ClearMind
projects.blurb: Five minutes of thinking practice a day. Everyone gets the same puzzles on the same date, so you can compare your judgement against yesterday's and against other people's.
projects.readmeBlurb: A 5-minute daily mental-exercise web app — calibration, estimation, and a daily intention, instead of scrolling. Built like Wordle: a deterministic daily seed derived from the date generates the same session for everyone, with no backend.

projects.title: Fractal Universe
projects.blurb: Fly out to a galaxy, pick a star, drop into its system, then land and walk on a planet that generates its terrain, water and wildlife as you arrive.
projects.readmeBlurb: An infinite, deterministic procedural universe in the browser. Fly through a galaxy of stars, drop into a star system, and descend to walk or fly on a procedurally generated planet surface with terrain, water, plants, herds, and flocking birds. Every location is a pure function of a single seed, so the same URL always reproduces the same world — on any machine.

projects.title: Python Interview Trainer
projects.blurb: Learn Python in small steps, then practise on interview-style problems. Your code actually runs in the browser, so there's nothing to install.
projects.readmeBlurb: A single-page web app that teaches Python as a curriculum: short lessons introduce each concept in small, low-stakes steps, then interview-style problems let you apply it. Runs Python in the browser via Pyodide — no backend needed.

projects.title: Hex Hive Drop
projects.blurb: Tetris on a hexagonal hive that rotates under you. Gravity follows the glowing wall, so the board you were planning for keeps turning.

projects.title: Love of Wisdom
projects.blurb: A map of philosophy organised by question rather than by philosopher, so you can see where thinkers who never met landed on the same answer.
projects.readmeBlurb: A question-first map of philosophical positions across traditions. The unit is the position, not the thinker and not the tradition, and the distinctive surface is the intersection view: where thinkers from traditions that never met turn out to have landed on the same answer — and where that resemblance turns out to be an artifact of the English word used for both.

projects.title: Duʿāʾ of the Prophets
projects.blurb: Sixty-three supplications from the Qur'an and authenticated Sunnah, each with the Arabic, a transliteration, a translation and the moment it was said.

projects.title: SoundScope
projects.blurb: Turn your phone into a sound-level meter and find out whether the room you're in is quietly damaging your hearing. Installs as an app, works offline.
projects.readmeBlurb: A browser-based sound-level meter and hearing-awareness toolkit. It runs entirely on your device, works offline (installable PWA), and is free to host on GitHub Pages. No accounts, no servers, no tracking, no ads.

projects.title: The Flashes
projects.blurb: An English-language companion to Lem'alar by Said Nursî — full text, search, cross-references and notes, for readers coming to it without Ottoman Turkish.
projects.readmeBlurb: An independent companion and study guide for Lem'alar ("The Flashes") by Bediüzzaman Said Nursî — one of the books of the Risale-i Nur collection. Built for English-speaking readers who want to understand, navigate, search and remember this dense work.

projects.title: Truth · Ethics · Benefit
projects.blurb: A working tool for deliberating hard decisions: weigh what's true, what's right and what actually helps, and see where those three pull apart.
projects.readmeBlurb: This application implements the framework defended in the working paper Truth, Ethics, and Benefit: A Multi-Source Framework for Practical Deliberation by Umut Candan. The framework argues that truth-judgment, ethical-judgment, and benefit-judgment are three irreducible moments of one deliberative act, integrated through the agent's intentional orientation, operating within four mutually necessary but asymmetrically ordered sources: revelation (waḥy), reason (ʿaql), sense-experience (tajriba), and conscience (qalb / ḍamīr).

projects.title: Earth Sim
projects.blurb: Take charge of a country and see what your policy choices do to its people, its economy and its neighbours over the following decades.
projects.description: a simulation game where you control a country
projects.readmeBlurb: A real-time-with-pause world conquest game in the browser. You pick a country in 1900 and try to bring 60 % of the world's population under your colors — through war, alliances, gifts, and tech. Other countries don't wait for you; each one runs on its own personality and acts whether you intervene or not.

projects.title: The Complete Human

projects.readmeBlurb: An evidence-based personal development platform. A daily-use tool that helps you practice, track, and compound small improvements across 8 interdependent life dimensions backed by behavioral science.

projects.title: AdilStore
projects.blurb: A small app store for software that doesn't harvest you — handpicked tools, mindful games and spiritual companions, with the privacy terms stated up front.
projects.readmeBlurb: The entire product is one HTML file (3,062 lines) — index.html. It contains inline CSS, inline JavaScript as an ES module, bilingual translations, 47 hardcoded apps, Supabase client config, all UI logic, and all rendering. It is hosted on GitHub Pages. There is no build system, no package manager, no tests, no CI, no deployment pipeline.
